scope: Paired SIMLOX 2017 CLI comparison of BIG48P5.PMRID null versus CAL24 while the sole P-MAINT worker is expected to be performing one second-cycle CAL24 subtask at the larger PM due. Establish native event ordering and whether already-performing or waiting small-PM work stops.

dependency.accepted_behavior: BIG47 starts on both aircraft at 47; unlinked second-cycle CAL24 works 49-51, linked has one CAL24 absent and one stopped before work; one shared worker. This follow-on changes larger-PM due time to cross a smaller-PM work episode.

manual.rule: MaterielPM.PMRID identifies a more frequent smaller PM included in the current PM. Native event logs must decide how an already active small PM is treated; do not assume that a task in performance can stop.

frozen_source_delta: For each arm, derive directly from its accepted D12.var01 v1.0.1 input; keep seed1, one replication, 60-hour horizon, three missions, two aircraft, one shared worker, CAL24 ENREG=Y and all other source rows.
Change the sole larger PM PMID BIG47 to BIG48P5, DESCR and PMINT 47 to 48.5; update its PMLocation and PM-BIG47 task references to PM-BIG48P5, plus ProblemDescription.
Between new arms, only descriptive text and BIG48P5.PMRID null versus CAL24 differ.
acceptance_hypotheses: Before 48.5, the paired arms have identical native event traces. At least one CAL24 second-cycle subtask starts performing at hour 48 and is still performing when BIG48P5 becomes due at hour 48.5; confirm these conditions from native logs before interpreting PMRID behavior.

A PMRID-linked larger PM may cancel an already-performing or waiting smaller PM; the exact ordering, task status, worker release, and any completed work must be measured, not assumed. If no differential behavior appears, record a diagnostic rather than claiming interruption.

Both arms retain all authored populated cells through native import/export, zero converter errors and usable outputs. Event PM/worker ledgers reconcile with 120 half-hour System/Resource/Stock bins and terminal state.
gate: Accept only an observed pairwise PMRID effect on a small PM that was physically performing at the larger PM due, after exact source diff, zero converter errors, valid simulation output, event/worker/report reconciliation and separate read-only replay. If the exposure or differential effect is absent, preserve the immutable run as a diagnostic and revise a new version; do not publish an interruption claim.
execution_guard: Session-0 SSH with sshd ancestor, Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue, GUI PID 13340/session 1 active and identity-preserved, immutable run path, 60-second targeted child watchdog, source/tool hashes before/after and raw SHA-256 closure.
limits: One two-aircraft system, one seed, one base, one shared worker and one CALHOURS relation; no general PMRID scheduling, multi-level PM, ENFNC, remote-base PM, GUI or cross-engine claim.
Native logs may not expose PM counter reset values; any such interpretation must remain a limit unless direct evidence is found.
